properties.Name: Col. Samuel W. Peel House
properties.NatID: This museum was built by Samuel W. Peel in 1875. The Italianate Villa style features an outdoor area containing perennials and native plants in gardens exhibiting walkways and shade trees. In addition to the pre-civil war, Andy Lunch Log Cabin.

properties.Name: Maxwell-Hinman House
properties.NatID: This is a high style Italianate dwelling originally done in red brick. The ornamentation includes corner quoin-work, window hood moulds, and roof bracketing all made of brick.

properties.Name: Linebarger House
properties.NatID: This is a splendid example of the Bungalow form with tapering rock columns and a wide roof overhang. The expanded use of rough fieldstone is unusual in a house of this carefully crafted design.

properties.Name: Macon Harrison House
properties.NatID: This structure was built by John Macon, a partner in the Macon & Carson Distillery of apple brandy. The bold use of rusticated limestone in the quoins, belt course, lintels, and porch columns indicates excellent craftsmanship.

properties.Name: Bentonville Train Station
properties.NatID: This one-story structure has exterior brick walls covered with stucco. A bay window projects from the track side. A flat room spans the structure with a parapet wall topped by a white capstone. It currently houses the Bentonville History Museum.

properties.Name: Elliott House
properties.NatID: This high-style house includes an elaborate Victorian mixture of Italianate, Second Empire, and Queen Anne features. Multi-colored plan flooring is only one element of its imaginative interior.

properties.Name: Col Young House
properties.NatID: The original porches have been removed. A one-story brick kitchen still remains in the rear. It is probably the earliest of Bentonville’s Italianate homes.

properties.Name: Terry Block Building
properties.NatID: This commercial building was originally built in 1888 by Col. William A. Terry as a dry goods store. The front corner was occupied by the Benton County Bank. The walls included white limestone lintel blocks and windowsills.

properties.Name: Benton County Jail
properties.NatID: This New-Classic structure, designed by A.O. Clark of Rogers, built by Lon Clark. 6 cell blocks held 4 prisoners each, and there were rooms for the jailer’s family. The Quorum Court mandated the sheriff live on site after the previous jail was set fire.

properties.Name: Benton County Courthouse
properties.NatID: This three-story Neo-Classic style structure was designed by A.O. Clark late in his career. The cost in 1928 was just over $200,000.

properties.Name: Benton County National Bank
properties.NatID: This bank was also designed by A.O. Clark and it is characterized by its Roman Temple Form embellished by red granite columns. Much interior woodwork is original.

properties.Name: Bentonville High School (Old High)
properties.NatID: The school was designed by John Park Almand in the Spanish Colonial style. It is now functioning as Old High Middle School. The auditorium of the site has been restored.

properties.Name: Bentonville Post Office
properties.NatID: The Robinson Hotel stood on this site in 1892. In 1908, a brick building was erected as the US Agriculture Weather Station for the apple growers of the area. In 1925, the current structure was built as the US Post Office.

properties.Name: Craig Bryan House
properties.NatID: This imposing house has an Italian Villa-style tower. The iron balconies on the front are from the 1874 brick courthouse that stood on the northwest corner of the square for many years.

properties.Name: Massey Hotel
properties.NatID: A.O. Clark designed this building on the original site of the 1840 Eagle Hotel. In the past 110+ years, it has housed hotel guests, a train ticket office, radio station, barber shop, gift shop, Public Library, and Phat Tire.

properties.Name: Braithwaite House
properties.NatID: This house was built for John Breathwaite by James Haney. It features one story, a central hall, a classic example of the residential form in pre-Civil War homes. The owners had extensive orchards and developed the Arkansas black Apple.

properties.Name: Benton County Poor Farm Cemetery
properties.Address: West side of NE Young, 200 ft N of NE Carnahan Court
